synopsis: Chapter 10 identifies Sandia’s Predictive Capability Maturity Model (PCMM; Oberkampf et al., 2007) as a literature-cited decision model for verification, validation and uncertainty quantification maturity, but says it was not separately verified [f7721, f7722]. Chapter 12 compares PCMM with NASA 7009B, ASME V&V 40 and UNECE NATM, dating their origins to 2007, 2024, 2018 and 2022–2024 respectively [f10025]. For the collision-mitigation virtual-testing toolchain, the planning recommendation is to replace TRLs with a credibility maturity scale, specifically NASA-STD-7009B or Sandia PCMM (SAND2007-5948) [f9536, f10031]. The stated rationale is that these frameworks assess simulation maturity, fit high uncertainty with a fixed deadline, and respond to blind-prediction gaps [f10026, f10027, f10028]. The assessment favors documented practice, while acknowledging that the frameworks are “largely declarative”; this and PCMM’s lack of separate verification qualify the recommendation [f10030, f10029, f7722].
